newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa's pneumonia worries doctors.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa's pneumonia worries doctors.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Sunday the 86-year-old nun had suffered a setback in her recovery from pneumonia and they were concerned about her unstable condition.
They said the Roman Catholic missionary was suffering from bronchial pneumonia which had not yet responded to antibiotics or respiratory treatment. She would stay at least another week in hospital.
"There seems to have been some sort of setback," A.K. Chatterjee, an administrator at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, told a news conference.

Mother Teresa underwent surgery on November 29 to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She appeared to be recovering normally, despite an irregular heartbeat, when long-standing lung and kidney problems resurfaced.
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner also contracted bronchial pneumonia, which doctors have been treating with antibiotics. Every six hours they have removed fluid which has collected in her lungs.
On Sunday, they said the measures to check the pneumonia had not been as effective as they hoped.
"Today it is not as good as yesterday," Chatterjee said.
"Mother Teresa's condition is not stable as yet," doctors treating the renowned nun said in a regular bulletin on her condition. "Physicians remain concerned."
They added: "She continues with chest congestion due to bronchial pneumonia in spite of aggressive respiratory and antibiotic therapy."
Chatterjee did not indicate what type of setback Mother Teresa had suffered.
On Saturday, doctors delayed a procedure to correct her irregular heartbeat because they wanted to wait until she was stronger.
The procedure, known as cardioversion, involves drugs or a mild electric shock, doctors said. "It has been put on hold for at least another two days," Chatterjee said.
He added that there was no chance Mother Teresa would soon be able to resume her work with the poor and the sick. "We will keep her here for at least another week," he said.
The bulletin said Mother Teresa's kidneys had returned to normal, though her heartbeat remained irregular.
"Her cardiac status is stabilising, but requires close monitoring," it said. "Mother is still not out of danger."
Doctors have warned that Mother Teresa's recovery will take a long time and have said she might never be as active as before.
